reasons: Several hint texts are hardcoded to the recorded story, so they will mislead if the story changes.
No tests are visible for this file.
Some text branches assume particular data shapes, such as money values in millions.

terms.meaning: A read-only guided tour of recorded example data, separate from the live workspace.
A short guidance box with a title, text and optional buttons.
The recorded example: a fixed set of signals, filters and a prepared question.
A sourced finding about the market, such as news of a project or problem, that the tool tracks.
The rulebook that classifies signals into solutions, triggers, types, industries and themes.
The project records this app links signals to.
Values passed into a component by its parent, such as hint or onDismiss.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for demo hints
sections.what: Brings in the shared building blocks the hints need: links, icons, data types, the storyline, filter helpers and the score function.
sections.why: Setup code for the rest of the file.

sections.name: HintAction, Hint
sections.title: Shape of a guidance hint
sections.what: Defines what one hint contains: a button label, click action and test id for each button, and a hint with an id, title, body text and optional buttons.
sections.why: A shared shape lets every hint be shown by the same box on screen.
sections.watch_out: Each hint id must be unique, because dismissal is remembered by id.

sections.name: DemoHint
sections.title: Showing and dismissing one hint
sections.what: Draws one hint box with a Demo tag, the title, the text, its buttons and a close X. It draws nothing when there is no hint. Pressing X reports the hint's id back to the parent.
sections.why: Lets visitors read guidance without leaving the page, and dismiss what they do not need.
sections.watch_out: Dismissed hints come back after a page reload, because the dismissed list lives only in page memory.

sections.name: DemoBadge, plural, short, isLinked
sections.title: Demo banner and small helpers
sections.what: DemoBadge draws the top banner that says the data is recorded and read-only, with buttons to hide or show hints and to leave the demo. The helpers format counts with singular or plural words, shorten long text with an ellipsis, and check whether a signal is linked to a Yard project.
sections.why: Likely reason: the banner tells visitors what they are looking at, and the helpers keep the hint wording consistent.
sections.watch_out: A signal counts as linked when its Yard status is linked, matched or created, so a change to those statuses changes the hint wording.

sections.name: DemoCtx, inStory, opened, accountName
sections.title: Shared demo context and story checks
sections.what: The context type bundles everything hints read. Other helpers check whether the industry filter is the LNG storyline, find the pre-opened signal, and get the pinned account's name.
sections.why: Keeps the hint functions short by sharing these lookups.
sections.watch_out: If the pinned signal is removed from saved data, the lookup returns nothing and hints fall back to generic text.

sections.name: startHint
sections.title: Main hint for the LNG view
sections.what: Writes the top hint for the LNG storyline or the pinned account. It gives counts of signals, how many are classified as LNG and how many are linked to Yard, and offers buttons to ask the prepared question, open the account, open the linked signal, or return to the LNG view. Outside the LNG industry it shows a neutral note.
sections.why: Likely reason: the first hint a visitor sees should explain the recorded example and suggest a route through it.
sections.watch_out: The ask button only appears when a recorded answer exists, and the account text is built from the first matching signal only.

sections.name: viewHint
sections.title: Hints for each analysis tab
sections.what: Returns a hint for the open analysis tab: geography (which Gulf Coast signals have locations), regions (how many problem signals are linked), solution and trigger views, the priority ranking, capex, and the codebook-driven views. Hidden when the account filter is on or the industry is not LNG.
sections.why: Likely reason: each tab needs a short explanation of what it shows for the recorded example.
sections.watch_out: Several names are typed into the text, such as the Gulf Coast locations and the Energia Costa Azul signal, so if the recorded story changes this text will be wrong.

sections.name: detailHint
sections.title: Hint for the opened and linked signals
sections.what: For the pre-opened signal, explains its sources and publishers, its tier reason, and whether it has a location. For the signal linked to the pinned account, explains the Yard link. Returns nothing for other signals.
sections.why: Likely reason: helps visitors understand evidence and classification on the signal they are most likely to open.
sections.watch_out: The tier explanation shows only the first recorded reason, so other reasons are not shown.

sections.name: projectsHint
sections.title: Hint for project news and profiles
sections.what: On the LNG news page, counts dated events and upcoming milestones since the feed start date, and states that an empty list is a recording gap rather than proof of no news. On the profiles page, describes the opened project's planned and actual capex and its delay.
sections.why: Likely reason: the caveat about empty lists stops visitors reading a gap as evidence that nothing happened.
sections.watch_out: Money values are assumed to be in millions and are divided by 1,000 to show billions, so a change in units would show wrong figures. The caveat is fixed text and is not checked against whether the feed was complete.

sections.name: codebookHint
sections.title: Codebook summary hint
sections.what: Counts the solutions, trigger families, signal types, industries and themes in the codebook, and states that demo edits stay in the session and do not change the shared codebook or re-classify signals.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains that the codebook can be viewed and edited in the demo without affecting real data.
sections.watch_out: The counts update live, but the sentence about demo edits is fixed text and must be edited by hand if the editing rules change.

summary: Creates the guided hints shown in the Opportunity Map demo, using only the saved LNG storyline data, so each hint's numbers come from the same data the tool shows.
purpose: Guides a demo visitor through the recorded LNG example by explaining what they see and suggesting the next click.
why: The file header says every number is computed at display time so a hint cannot drift from the tool. The reason for the demo itself is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Hints are plain objects with an id, title, body and optional buttons. 2. Each hint function looks at the current filters, view, selected signal, page, or loaded data. 3. It returns a hint or nothing. 4. DemoHint draws the hint box with a dismiss button. 5. DemoBadge draws the top banner with show or hide and leave-demo controls.
inputs: The demo context (saved data, scoped signals, filters, weights, name and label lookups), the current view or page, the open signal, the project feed, and the codebook.
outputs: Hint objects, which DemoHint draws on screen, and a banner for the demo header.
risks: Some wording names specific recorded items, such as Gulf Coast locations, the Energia Costa Azul signal and the Chevron project. If the storyline data changes, these hints can describe the wrong thing. Dismissed hints are stored only in page memory.
debug: If a hint is missing, check the filters and the view name it is looking for; most hints return nothing outside the LNG industry. If a count is wrong, compare with the same filter on the main page. If a button does nothing, check the matching action passed in from index.tsx.
